title: Microsurgical technique for femoral vascular access in the rat
author: Ghali

steps.title: Prepare catheter tubing and stopcock
steps.instruction: Cut PE50 tubing to ~20 cm and bevel the tip at a 45° angle with a razor blade; secure the tubing over a needle attached to a three‑way stopcock; connect the two remaining ports to syringes (one 1 ml syringe filled with 300 U/L heparin in Ringer‑Locke for the arterial line, and 5 ml syringes filled with normal saline, Ringer‑Locke, or artificial CSF). Fill the arterial catheter system with the heparinized solution and the venous system with non‑heparinized solution, then lock the stopcock toward the catheter tubing.

substeps.instruction: Cut PE50 tubing (~20 cm) and bevel tip (45°).
Attach tubing to needle on three‑way stopcock.
Connect syringes: 1 ml heparinized (300 U/L) for artery; 5 ml saline/Ringer‑Locke/CSF for other ports.
Fill arterial line with heparinized solution; fill venous line with non‑heparinized solution.

steps.title: Induce anesthesia and monitor ECG
steps.instruction: Place the rat (340–380 g) in a snout mask; induce anesthesia with isoflurane in O₂ at 4–5% then maintain at 1.85–2.15%; insert three subcutaneous electrodes and monitor the ECG with amplification, an audio amplifier, and an oscilloscope; maintain depth such that withdrawal reflexes and heart‑rate responses to distal hind‑limb pinches are absent.

steps.title: Incise skin and expose femoral bundle
steps.instruction: Make a skin incision parallel to the femoral sheath; bluntly dissect soft tissue to expose the femoral neurovascular bundle; open the femoral sheath by blunt dissection along its long axis between the femoral artery (lateral) and vein (medial); further separate the vessels with blunt dissection.

steps.title: Apply distal ligation to femoral vein
steps.instruction: Place a 4‑0 braided silk suture around the femoral vein distal to the vena profunda femoris and tie a knot; thread the suture ends through a needle holder (or hemostat) positioned ~3 cm from the knot and let the holder rest on the edge of the operating table, forming an approximate 30° angle with the horizontal to provide gentle tension on the vessel.

steps.title: Establish proximal control of femoral vein
steps.instruction: Apply a temporary vascular clip immediately distal to the vena profunda femoris to achieve proximal control.

steps.title: Create venotomy and insert venous catheter
steps.instruction: Using iridectomy scissors, make a 1–2 mm venotomy 1–2 mm proximal to the distal ligation, cutting the upper half of the vessel circumference at a 45° angle; open the stopcock toward the catheter, depress a syringe to generate a fluid bubble at the catheter tip; insert the catheter through the venotomy and advance it until it contacts the vascular clip; lock the stopcock toward the catheter.

steps.title: Advance and secure venous catheter
steps.instruction: Remove the vascular clip, advance the catheter distally to the level of the inguinal ligament, and secure it to the femoral vein proximally and distally with three single 4‑0 silk knots.

steps.title: Confirm venous catheter patency
steps.instruction: Unlock the catheter, withdraw approximately 0.2 ml of venous blood, then flush the line with about 1 ml of saline (or the chosen solution).

steps.title: Ligate and transect lymphatic duct
steps.instruction: Ligate the lymphatic duct proximally and distally with 4‑0 silk, transect it with iridectomy scissors, and inspect the field for any lymphatic leakage; if leakage is observed, re‑ligate the individual ends.

steps.title: Apply distal ligation to femoral artery
steps.instruction: After lateral retraction of the femoral artery to expose the arteria profunda femoris, place a 4‑0 silk suture distal to this branch, tie a knot, and apply the same tension method using a needle holder ~3 cm from the knot at a ~30° angle.

steps.title: Establish proximal control of femoral artery
steps.instruction: Apply a temporary vascular clip immediately distal to the arteria profunda femoris.

steps.title: Create arteriotomy and insert arterial catheter
steps.instruction: Make a 1–2 mm arteriotomy 1–2 mm proximal to the distal ligation; fill the open arterial catheter with heparinized Ringer‑Locke (300 U/L); open the stopcock toward the catheter, insert the catheter, and advance it to the vascular clip; lock the stopcock toward the catheter.

steps.title: Advance and secure arterial catheter
steps.instruction: Remove the vascular clip, advance the catheter to the inguinal ligament, and secure it proximally and distally with three single 4‑0 silk knots.

steps.title: Confirm arterial catheter patency
steps.instruction: Unlock the catheter and observe arterial pulsations at the catheter tip; optionally withdraw a small blood sample and flush a similar volume, noting that added heparin may cause mild coagulopathy.

steps.title: Replace tissue bulk and close incision
steps.instruction: Place a Ringer‑Locke‑soaked cottonoid in the femoral region to replace removed soft tissue; close the skin incision with continuous 4‑0 braided silk suture to prevent fluid loss and leakage.
